newsitem.title: USA: Dade County, Fla., okays seaport planning contract.
newsitem.headline: Dade County, Fla., okays seaport planning contract.

text.p: Florida's Dade County Commission approved a $303,000 architecture contract for proposed expansion at the Port of Miami despite questions raised by some officials about the project's feasibility.

The Maritime Park master plan contract with the firm Cooper, Robertson & Partners was approved retroactively Tuesday night. The firm has already begun work on the plans and billed the county for $100,000.

The project would be financed with $48 million of seaport revenue bonds and would add at least two new cruise ship berths. It would include a basketball arena to be financed by the Miami Heat and possibly shopping and entertainment facilities.
Funding for the proposal was in doubt after a county audit revealed the seaport has a $22 million deficit, and had been subsidized with general fund revenues for several years.

Commissioner Jimmy Morales, who chairs the commisson's finance committee, said completing the master plan would not tie the county to building the park, but would enable it to move quickly if the money is found.
"We want to make sure that before we issue one more bond at the seaport, before we incur that debt, the money is going to be there," Morales said.
The architecture firm began the work before the commission approved the contract because the county's contract with the Heat required the master plan, county officials said.
The architecture contract was approved despite objections that the plan would not address the impact on poor neighborhoods near the downtown project.
Additionally, the county is still in negotiations with the City of Miami to buy or lease the waterfront site, but the two remain far apart on the price.

"A retroactive project with a future funding source isn't really the way we ought to be doing business," said Commissioner Katy Sorenson, who voted against the expenditure. "It's a partial plan for money that we don't have for land that we don't have either."
